references.text: Moses had previously demanded that they take their flocks and herds when they went to worship the Lord, something Pharaoh now finally agrees to.
Moses insisted that all the livestock must go with them, for they did not know what they would need for sacrifices until they arrived.
Pharaoh commanded Moses and Aaron to leave with the children of Israel, and this verse continues with permission to take their livestock.
Esau asked his father Isaac for a blessing, in the same way that Pharaoh asks for a blessing from Moses.
Jacob blessed Pharaoh when he came to Egypt, and now this Pharaoh asks for a blessing from Moses as the Israelites leave the land.
Balak knew that whoever Moses blessed was blessed, showing the power of blessings from God's servants.
Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, an example of how men of God bless others.
A direct continuation of the same sequence of events where Pharaoh changes strategy from keeping the animals as hostages to asking for a blessing.
